user.title: Venus Surplus Control
user.description: The entities of your Marstek Venus are filled in from the Marstek Venus Modbus integration where they are found; check them and correct any that does not fit. Then pick the sensor that gives your PV surplus. Everything can be changed later under Configure.

data.name: Name
data.surplus_entity: Surplus sensor (PV production minus house consumption, W)
data.surplus_invert: The surplus sensor is a grid meter with import positive
data.venus_ac_invert: AC power is negative while the Venus delivers into the house

data_description.surplus_entity: PV production minus house consumption in W, positive while there is surplus. A grid meter works too: tick the box below if it is positive while importing.

optional.title: Optional inputs and limits
optional.description: Leave empty what you do not have. Without a first battery the Venus is the only storage; without a forecast the first battery always goes first.

data.primary_power_invert: First battery power is positive while charging
data.modbus_entry_id: Marstek Venus Modbus config entry (for the self-heal reload)
data.primary_missing_alone: Carry on without the first battery when its readings are missing

data_description.primary_reserve_entity: Optional. The charge level at which your inverter stops discharging the first battery. The Venus then treats it as empty 3 points above that (at least 12 %). Without it, a fixed 12 % applies.
data_description.discharge_limit_w: What the Venus can deliver at most (Venus A 1000 W; raise it for a D or E). A feed-in limit below lowers it further.
data_description.feed_in_limit: What a plug-in device may deliver into the house wiring. Applies to discharging only, charging is not limited. The integration caps the discharge command and, on a Venus with its own PV, the measured AC delivery, so that PV and battery together stay below the limit. Check the rules that apply to your installation.
data_description.venus_pv_entities: Only for a Venus with its own PV inputs (A, D). Leave empty for a C or E.
data_description.forecast_factor: The remaining forecast is multiplied by this before it is compared with what both batteries still need. Below 1 is cautious.
data_description.ac_charge_limit_w: The highest charge command the integration sends.
data_description.total_charge_limit_w: Charge command plus the Venus' own PV together. Without own PV set it to the same value as the AC charge limit.
data_description.tick_seconds: How often the controller decides. Shorter reacts faster, longer is calmer. The values you tune (charge from surplus of, charging buffer, reaction) are on the device page under Configuration, not here.
data_description.primary_missing_alone: Off: while the power or SoC of the first battery is unavailable, the controller sends no commands and puts the Venus into standby. On: after 5 minutes without readings it runs the Venus alone, as if no first battery were set up, and goes back as soon as the readings return. For a first battery you switch off now and then. Leave it off if your surplus sensor is a grid meter and the battery may keep working while its sensors are gone: the Venus could then discharge into it.

inputs_missing.title: Venus Surplus Control: readings incomplete
inputs_missing.description: The controller has had no complete readings for several minutes and sends no commands (after two such ticks it puts the Venus into standby). Missing or unavailable: {entities}. Check the Marstek Venus Modbus integration and the surplus sensor, or pick other entities under Configure. This notice disappears as soon as the readings are complete again.

primary_missing.title: Venus Surplus Control: first battery without readings
primary_missing.description: The first battery has delivered no readings for 5 minutes ({entities}). As chosen under Configure, the controller runs the Venus alone until they return: it charges from any surplus and discharges against house demand, and the rules that coordinate the two batteries are off. This notice disappears as soon as the readings are back.
